reuse.why: Holidays are threaded through the existing applyWeekendRule and a new shared isNonWorkingDay, but the daily-skip variant is decided outside that rule, so callers re-derive it instead of reusing one definition.

duplication.why: The condition skipWeekend && frequency === 'daily' and the skip-vs-move branching appear in getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and schedule-template, and getDatesInRange restates getUpcomingDates' per-date branch.

placement.why: Day classification lives in shared/schedules.ts where the weekend rule lives, but the policy of which mode applies (skip for daily, move otherwise) is spread across server handlers and the budget template module.

scope.why: Changes correspond to the four steps (type, release notes, rule-utils data, handler); only minor noise such as `movesWeekends ? true : false`.

maintainability.why: The comment still calls applyWeekendRule 'the single definition of the weekend rule', yet four call sites each decide when the daily-skip mode overrides it, so a change to that policy must be made in several places that already differ in shape.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange (server/schedules/app.ts) and createScheduleList (server/budget/schedule-template.ts) branch on frequency === 'daily' themselves around applyWeekendRule instead of the rule deciding skip vs move.

disguised_duplication.where: getDatesInRange re-expresses getUpcomingDates' skip-or-apply-weekend-rule logic as a for-loop over a Set rather than sharing it; the daily-skip test is restated as skipsWeekends / movesWeekends / inline conditions.

abstraction_drift.where: applyWeekendRule/getDateWithSkippedWeekend gain a holidays parameter; getNextDate (shared/schedules.ts) gains a daily-skip special-case branch; getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and schedule-template's createScheduleList each decide the daily-skip mode outside the rule.
